justification: Corrects a declared status in two ledger files (DATA_QUALITY_TRACKER.md, dq_checks.json) from 'fixed' to 'open' to match the live check's actual result. No code path, no schema, no served value, no production write -- documentation-and-declaration only, verified against a live read-only check.

falsifiable_check.fails_when: DQ-79 is declared 'fixed' while dq_probe_live.py --id DQ-79 returns nonzero (the exact mismatch that was blocking every open PR's gate today), or declared 'open' while the probe returns 0 (which would hide a real fix behind a stale open status).
falsifiable_check.observed_red: Before this change: 'RED DQ-79: declared FIXED but the check FAILS', 'DQ-CHECK: FAILED', 1 red of 91 rows. After: '0 red', 'DQ-CHECK: PASSED' -- same live database state, only the declared status changed, confirming the ratchet was reacting to the declaration/reality mismatch specifically, not to the underlying data problem (which remains genuinely open).

pre_impl.existing_data: dcp_chapter_registry id 257 (ku_ring_gai/section-a-part-8-mixed-use), url_content_length=1, checked 2026-09-01 02:04 UTC. Read-only: queried via scripts/dq_db.py's read-only session, no write to this or any other row.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: Assumed initially this might be the same Hornsby row from the 08-15 fix, reoccurring as a regression. Verified false by querying the live row directly -- it is a different council and chapter entirely, and the 08-15 code fix (Content-Range parsing in head_request()) is confirmed still present and correctly working against this new row's URL.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Applies only to the DQ-79 ledger entry's declared status; no other row's status touched.

values.nullable: no, always one of a small enum (fixed/open/etc)
values.guard_at: dq_check.py's own comparison against the probe's live exit code
values.if_missing: n/a -- this commit sets it explicitly, does not remove it

queries.purpose: identify which specific row is currently failing DQ-79's probe, and confirm it is not the row the 08-15 fix addressed
queries.file_line: ad-hoc read-only query via scripts/dq_db.py, mirroring dq_probe_live.py's own DQ-79 SQL
queries.where_clause: dcp_chapter_registry WHERE is_active AND url_content_length IS NOT NULL AND url_content_length < 1000
queries.if_zero: would mean the probe should already be green -- it was not, confirming a real row was failing
queries.if_wrong: returned exactly 1 row (id 257), matching the probe's own reported count of 1

break_it.scenario: The ledger correction is used to permanently paper over a live data defect instead of tracking it.
break_it.what_happens: DQ-79 would sit 'open' forever with nobody acting on the underlying Ku-ring-gai row.
break_it.how: The note explicitly states the row will likely self-correct on the chapter monitor's next scheduled run now that runners are back online, and flags a manual investigation as the fallback if it does not -- this is a status correction, not a closure.
break_it.repro: python scripts/dq_probe_live.py --id DQ-79 remains the live source of truth; re-run it after the monitor's next cycle to confirm it returns to 0

post_merge.manual_verify: Re-run python scripts/dq_probe_live.py --id DQ-79 after the chapter monitor's next scheduled cycle to confirm the Ku-ring-gai row self-corrected; if not, that is a genuine follow-up (a backed-up, WHERE-scoped UPDATE on dcp_chapter_registry id 257, or investigation into why the monitor isn't rechecking it).
